Welcome to this page for new staff, and read it as though every word is time-sensitive because it is. Topic: Companion Animal Travel Desk incident response and reporting. This matters because companion animal journeys demand safety first, clear coordination, and immediate escalation when anything threatens the passenger, the pet, or the flight operation.

You are part of a single chain of responsibility inside Aurelia Skyways, and the chain only works when you act consistently under pressure. Begin every interaction with calm, concise guidance to travelers and their pets. If a traveler appears distressed, acknowledge the concern, keep instructions simple, and do not delay the next safety step. When a pet is involved, prioritize handling procedures and minimize stress; treat every signal, sound, and change in behavior as actionable information. If Arjun Wong or Caleb Brown is traveling with Simba, or any other companion animal, you must keep communication factual, courteous, and focused on what comes next.

For incident reporting, the Claim Adjudicator oversees the process for immediate documentation and escalation.

When an incident occurs, stop the situation from worsening before you document. Stabilize the cabin or ground area, secure the pet in the appropriate carrier state, and confirm that the traveler understands the instruction you are giving. Record the timeline in plain language while events are still fresh, capturing what staff observed, what the traveler reported, and what actions were taken. Use the same wording patterns every time, avoid emotional language, and ensure that the report is complete enough for follow-up without requiring you to be reached again.

After the report is submitted, maintain availability for clarification, coordinate with the senior coordinator on any operational constraints, and never close the matter in your mind until the desk confirms receipt and next steps. Remember, safety, accuracy, and urgency must guide every action you take.
